expected.insightNarrative:
Dashboard is a Radio Towers Dashboard for a telecommunications network: the capacity of the radio links in each area, the status of every link on a map, and the detail of each link. Selecting a bar filters the dashboard and selecting a link highlights it. The story is a network still largely in the planned and build stages, with a handful of 345 Mb/s links carrying the highest capacity.

Key insights
- The highest-capacity links carry 345.0 Mb/s: both ends of link 5576 in the South West (SN-100P equipment, Norm 3 LLP, operational), the source of link 12857 in Central West and both ends of link 12745 in Central East and North (Hitachi XR, Monucell, in build); most other links carry 54 or 160 Mb/s.
- Planned and build capacity dominate every area; only a few areas carry cancelled capacity.
- Every link in the detail table reports 100.0% availability, with distances from 1.4 to 12.3 miles.

Overview
Network overview: a stacked bar per area (47.5-122, 47.6-122, 47.7-122, 47.8-122, Central East, Central West, North, North East, North West, South, South West) showing the share of capacity in Mb/s by link status, from 0% to 100%. Planned (blue) and build (olive) capacity dominate; the largest labelled segments are 345.0 in area 47.8-122 and 283.3 in North East, and only a few areas carry cancelled (red) capacity.

Cell Map
A map of the links around Seattle and Bellevue towards Kent, each drawn as a line coloured by link status (planned, build, operational, operational backup, cancelled) and sized by capacity (54, 160 or 345 Mb/s). Build links in olive cover most of the map, with planned links in blue concentrated to the west and north.

Link Data
A table of links with link ID, site ID, capacity (Mb/s), frequency band (GHz), distance (miles) and availability (%). Links 1618 and 1627 to 1633 are listed, mostly at 54.0 Mb/s on the 5.3 or 16.5 GHz bands, one (1630) at 160.0 Mb/s, with distances from 1.4 to 12.3 miles and 100.0% availability throughout.
